objectives.description: Role and function of network components
Routers forward traffic between networks using a routing table
Layer 2 switches forward frames by MAC address; Layer 3 switches forward packets by IP address
Next-generation firewalls and intrusion prevention systems inspect traffic and block or flag threats
Access points provide wireless connectivity to a wired LAN
Controllers centralise policy and configuration, such as Cisco DNA Center and a wireless LAN controller
Endpoints are devices that originate and consume traffic, such as hosts, phones and printers
Servers host applications and services for clients
Power over Ethernet delivers power and data over the same cable run
Characteristics of network topology architectures
Two-tier architecture is a flat access layer over a single distribution or core layer
Three-tier architecture separates access, distribution and core roles
Spine-leaf connects every leaf to every spine for predictable latency
A WAN connects sites over distance using carrier infrastructure
A small office/home office typically uses one device performing several roles
On-premises and cloud describe where workloads and data physically live
Physical interface and cabling types
Single-mode fibre, multimode fibre and copper trade off distance, cost and light source
Ethernet shared media and point-to-point differ in how bandwidth is shared
Identify interface and cable issues such as collisions, errors, duplex mismatch and speed mismatch
Compare TCP to UDP across reliability, ordering and overhead
Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting
Describe private IPv4 addressing and the intent of the reserved ranges
Configure and verify IPv6 addressing and prefix
IPv6 address types
Unicast covers global, unique-local and link-local scopes
Anycast makes one address reachable from many locations
Multicast delivers one sender to many receivers by group membership
Modified EUI-64 derives an IPv6 interface identifier from a MAC address
Verify IP parameters for a client operating system such as Windows, macOS or Linux
Wireless principles
Nonoverlapping Wi-Fi channels, such as 1, 6 and 11, avoid co-channel interference
The SSID is the network name broadcast by an access point
Radio frequency behaviour including interference and signal characteristics
Encryption protects wireless traffic over the air
Virtualization fundamentals covering server virtualization, containers and VRFs
Switching concepts
MAC learning and aging is how a switch populates and expires table entries
Frame switching forwards a frame out the correct port
Frame flooding sends out all ports when the destination is unknown
The MAC address table maps destinations to learned ports
Configure and verify VLANs in the normal range spanning multiple switches
Access ports carry data and voice traffic for a single VLAN
The default VLAN exists on a switch out of the box
InterVLAN connectivity routes between VLANs via a Layer 3 device
Configure and verify interswitch connectivity
Trunk ports carry multiple VLANs over one link
802.1Q VLAN tagging frames with a VLAN identifier
The native VLAN crosses a trunk untagged
Configure and verify Layer 2 discovery protocols, CDP and LLDP
Configure and verify Layer 2 and Layer 3 EtherChannel using LACP
Basic operation of Rapid PVST+ Spanning Tree Protocol
Root port, root bridge and the other spanning tree port roles
Port states and whether each forwards or blocks
PortFast marks an edge port that cannot create a loop
Root guard, loop guard, BPDU filter and BPDU guard
Cisco wireless architectures and access point modes
Physical infrastructure connections of WLAN components, covering access points, controllers, access and trunk ports, and link aggregation groups
Network device management access via Telnet, SSH, HTTP, HTTPS, console, TACACS+ or RADIUS, and cloud-managed access
Interpreting the wireless LAN GUI configuration for client connectivity
Components of the routing table
Routing protocol code identifies how a route was learned
The prefix is the network portion of a routing table entry
The network mask states how much of the address is prefix
The next hop is the address traffic is forwarded to
Administrative distance expresses preference between sources of routes
The metric expresses cost within a single routing protocol
The gateway of last resort is the fallback when no route matches
How a router makes a forwarding decision by default
Longest prefix match selects the most specific route
Administrative distance is the first decision between routes
The routing protocol metric breaks the tie within one protocol
Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing
A default route matches anything not matched more specifically
A network route points at an entire subnet
A host route points at a single address
A floating static stays dormant via a higher administrative distance
Configure and verify single-area OSPFv2
Neighbour adjacencies form over hello and dead intervals
Point-to-point is an OSPF network type
Broadcast networks and DR/BDR election
Router ID selection
Purpose, functions and concepts of first hop redundancy protocols
Configure and verify inside source NAT using static mappings and address pools
Configure and verify NTP in client and server modes
The role of DHCP and DNS within the network
The function of SNMP in network operations
Syslog features including facilities and severity levels
Configure and verify DHCP client and relay
Per-hop behaviour for QoS: classification, marking, queuing, congestion, policing and shaping
Configure network devices for remote access using SSH
The capabilities and functions of TFTP and FTP in the network
Key security concepts: threats, vulnerabilities, exploits and mitigation techniques
Security program elements covering user awareness, training and physical access control
Configure and verify device access control using local passwords
Password policy elements: management, complexity, and alternatives such as multifactor authentication, certificates and biometrics
IPsec remote access and site-to-site VPNs
Configure and verify access control lists
Configure and verify Layer 2 security features: DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection and port security
Compare authentication, authorization and accounting concepts
Wireless security protocols: WPA, WPA2 and WPA3
Configure and verify a WLAN in the GUI using WPA2 PSK
How automation impacts network management
Compare traditional networks with controller-based networking
Controller-based software-defined architecture: overlay, underlay and fabric
Separation of the control plane and the data plane
Northbound and southbound APIs
Generative and predictive AI, and machine learning in network operations
Characteristics of REST-based APIs: authentication types, CRUD, HTTP verbs and data encoding
Capabilities of configuration management mechanisms such as Ansible and Terraform
Components of JSON-encoded data
